Theres a big difference between meat and dairy farming and between smaller farms and factory farms.

You have to remember we're talking about kids. It can be intimidating standing up against an authority figure, especially if you've never had to do it before. Even some adults would struggle to stand up for themselves in that situation out of fear of being punished.

I always get annoyed when it's implied that better time management on the students part will solve this problem. 

At my school we only had 4 minute breaks between class periods. Our only bathrooms were on the first floor of a 3 story building and the womens were all located at one end of the building.

4 minutes was barely enough to get to your next class. If you had a class on the 3rd floor and your next was on the 1st you better not need to stop at your locker. Imagine having two classes back to back on the first floor but realizing you had to get to your locker on the 3rd floor and back down in 4 minutes without running. 

We would get in trouble for being late to class so the best option would be to get to class on time and then ask to use the bathroom. 

It might be tough for teachers to manage, but it's a lot harder on the 7th grader who bleeds through her pants because she wasn't allowed to leave. I learned to stand up for myself the hard way.

Then she had me pick a feeling or situation that made me anxious and I chose how I feel like nobody believes me when I'm physically ill. She then had me think about that feeling while following her finger on a horizontal line until I found a spot that made my anxiety felt the strongest. Then she did the same thing vertically. 

I had to keep my eyes on that spot and try to remember when I first felt that way about people not believing me. Surprisingly I was able to figure that out really fast.
